_note: The ONLY legal provisions the bot may cite. Each entry was checked by a human against the listed sources on the date shown. To add a problem type, add entries here; nothing else changes.

laws.title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, Section 2(7): who is a 'consumer'
laws.plain: A person who buys goods or hires a service for payment, for their own use (not for resale or a commercial purpose), is a consumer. This includes online purchases.
laws.checked_against: Bare text of the Act, Section 2(7)

laws.title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, Section 2(10): 'defect'
laws.plain: A fault or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard of goods that the law, a contract or the seller's claim required.

laws.title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, Section 2(11): 'deficiency' in service
laws.plain: A fault or shortcoming in the quality or manner of a service, including negligence or deliberately withholding relevant information.

laws.title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, Section 2(47): 'unfair trade practice'
laws.plain: Includes misleading claims about goods or services and refusing to take back defective goods or refund within the stipulated or a reasonable period.
laws.caution: Whether the seller's conduct fits is for the Commission to decide.

laws.title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, Section 34 + Jurisdiction Rules, 2021: District Commission
laws.plain: The District Consumer Commission hears complaints where the price paid for the goods or service is up to Rs 50 lakh. You can usually file where you live or work, or where the seller does business.
laws.caution: The Rs 50 lakh limit comes from the Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction...) Rules, 2021 (notified 30 Dec 2021).
laws.official_source: India Code; Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of the District Commission, the State Commission and the National Commission) Rules, 2021

laws.title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, Section 35: how to file a complaint
laws.plain: A consumer can file a complaint with the District Commission, including electronically. In practice this is done on the e-Jagriti portal.

laws.title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, Section 69: time limit
laws.plain: A consumer complaint must be filed within 2 years from the date the problem (cause of action) arose. A late complaint is accepted only if the Commission accepts a good reason for the delay.
laws.caution: Exactly which date starts the 2 years can be argued; file early.

laws.title: Consumer Protection (Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions) Rules, 2020, Rule 7: filing fee
laws.plain: No fee if the price paid is up to Rs 5 lakh. Above that, a small fee that rises with the amount.

laws.title: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, Rule 4(5): grievance officer
laws.plain: Online shopping platforms must have a grievance officer who acknowledges a complaint within 48 hours and resolves it within one month.
laws.caution: Applies to e-commerce platforms and sellers, not to offline shops.

laws.title: Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 73: compensation for breach of contract
laws.plain: If someone breaks a contract (for example a rent agreement that says the deposit will be returned), the other side can claim compensation for the loss that naturally follows.

laws.title: Limitation Act, 1963: time limit for a civil suit to recover money
laws.plain: A civil suit to recover money (such as a deposit) generally has to be filed within about 3 years. When the 3 years start depends on the facts.
laws.caution: Sources and courts differ on WHICH article of the Limitation Act applies to a deposit claim (and so when time starts). Do not rely on this for a deadline; ask a lawyer if more than 2 years have passed.
laws.checked_against: Multiple secondary sources disagree; recorded as uncertain on purpose

laws.title: Model Tenancy Act, 2021, Section 11: security deposit
laws.plain: Under the Model Act, a residential deposit is capped at 2 months' rent and must be refunded when the landlord takes back vacant possession, after lawful deductions.
laws.caution: This is a MODEL law. It binds only in states that have passed a law based on it (for example Uttar Pradesh, 2021). Many states still use older rent laws. Always check your state.
laws.official_source: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs: Model Tenancy Act, 2021

laws.title: Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, Section 12: free legal aid
laws.plain: Some people are entitled to a free lawyer from the Legal Services Authority, including women, children, SC/ST persons, industrial workmen, persons with disabilities, people in custody and people under a state-set income limit.
laws.official_source: India Code: Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987

resources.name: National Consumer Helpline
resources.how: Call 1915 or 1800-11-4000 (8am-8pm, 17 languages), WhatsApp/SMS 8800001915, or consumerhelpline.gov.in. Free. Good first step before a formal complaint.

resources.name: e-Jagriti
resources.how: e-jagriti.gov.in: the official portal to file a consumer complaint online (replaced e-Daakhil from 1 Jan 2025).

resources.name: Free legal aid (NALSA / District Legal Services Authority)
resources.how: Call 15100 or visit the District Legal Services Authority at your district court. Free lawyer if you are eligible.

resources.name: Emergency
resources.how: Call 112 if you are in danger.
